newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS-Manila market ends slump but still suspect.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Manila market ends slump but still suspect.

text.p: The Philippine market, lifted by Dow Jones and a bounce in domestic property issues, climbed out of a two-day slump on Wednesday but remained vulnerable to speculative attacks, analysts said.
A day after taking its deepest plunge in 25 weeks, the key closed 53.11 points, or 1.86 percent higher, at 2,913.56 in what analysts said was a technical rebound. All sectors posted gains.
A total of 3.9 million shares changed hands, valued at a hefty 2.7 billion pesos, according to officially adjusted figures.
"The market just reacted to Wall Street's phenomenal rise and realisation that the fears on Empire and Megaworld were exaggerated," said Poch Zamora, dealer at Peregrine Securities.

Empire East Land Holdings Inc and parent firm Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc, which tumbled to lows for the year on Tuesday, bounced back on official company denials of rumours they were facing bankruptcy.
Megaworld closed at its session high of 4.80 pesos, rising 28 percent. Empire East, the most heavily traded issue, ended 30.14 percent at 4.75 pesos.
Analysts said Empire's announcement it was holding its annual stockholders meeting on Friday helped ease selling pressure on the rumour-battered stock.

"Probably if there are any more fears among investors, they would rather put off their selling orders for the meantime and listen to what they have to say," said Rolly Pineda, vice president of Tower Securities.
"I think the sustainability of the market's uptrend is still suspect," he said, adding there was still some selling pressure on issues like banks and real estate.
